thread:
alex_kim: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike of dropped east-west connections in eastus2 during nightly GPU job churn. Symptoms: pods = "connection reset by peer" to internal model-store and parameter-server services. Appears correlated with bursty outbound connections from inference pods.

maria_g: Thanks Alex. Any timing/metrics? CPU/memory ok?

alex_kim: CPU/RAM fine; latency graph shows a sudden increase in pod->pod retries and TCP resets around 03:10 UTC. Node-level dmesg shows nf_conntrack warnings on 3 gpunodes. Noticed a lot of SNAT entries on nodes.

vikram_s: Can you paste conntrack summary from one of the affected nodes?

alex_kim: Sure, from gpunode-12: 
```
# conntrack -S | egrep "entries|found"
cnf: table size = 65536
entries = 65122
found entries = 65122
cpu=0 flows: 60000
```
Also `ss -tan state established | wc -l` = 48k.

maria_g: 65k of 65k is basically full. Likely nf_conntrack_max hit and new connections get dropped -> TCP resets. Are these pods using hostNetwork or node SNAT?

irene_p: They are using default cluster networking (calico) with SNAT for pod egress. Ephemeral port space per node is finite so with many short lived connections we exhaust the SNAT mapping table.

jamie: Quick mitigation: increase nf_conntrack_max and ephemeral ports and shorten established timeout. E.g.: 
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"10240 61000\"
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600
```
That'll buy time but is bandaid.

vikram_s: Agree. Also check conntrack tcp states distribution (`conntrack -L | awk '{print $7}' | sort | uniq -c`) — tons of TIME_WAIT/ESTABLISHED could indicate many short connections or stuck flows.

alex_kim: Output: ESTABLISHED ~32k, TIME_WAIT ~18k, SYN_RECV ~1.5k.

maria_g: Could be clients retrying due to packet loss/fragmentation. Any MTU or RDMA changes recently? We rolled out jumbo MTU changes to two racks last week.

irene_p: Yep, eastus2 rack-3 had MTU lowered accidentally during maintenance (1500 -> 1400 mismatch between ToR and host NICs). That can cause fragmentation + retransmits. I'll open a ticket with network to verify.

jamie: If MTU mismatch, TCP retransmits increase connection churn -> more conntrack entries. Also RDMA traffic can exacerbate if fallback to TCP occurs.

vikram_s: Longer-term fixes: 1) Add pod-level connection pooling to reduce ephemeral conn count for model-store (we should reuse HTTP keepalive). 2) Move heavy egress to a NAT gateway per availability zone with higher capacity. 3) Consider NodeLocal SNAT (kube-proxy / CNI features) or eBPF-based SVC that reduces SNAT churn.

alex_kim: Action items I propose: 
- Irene: confirm MTU mismatch and coordinate rollback to 1500 on rack-3 (network)
- Jamie: apply temporary sysctl bump on affected nodes via an IMMEDIATE DaemonSet (nf_conntrack_max -> 180k, reduce tcp timeout to 300s)
- Maria/Vikram: add connection pooling / keepalive on model-store client side for next deploy
- Ops: provision extra NAT capacity in eastus2 if we still see high SNAT after fixes

irene_p: On it — pinged netops. Found interface errors on ToR switches consistent with MTU mismatch. Rolling back config now.

jamie: Preparing a small DaemonSet patch. Will run on gpunode-{12,13,14} first as canary. Command I'm applying: 
```
- name: sysctl-tune
  command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=180000 && sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300"]
```
Will report back after 5m.

alex_kim: Also raising kube-proxy log level to inspect SNAT mapping churn and enabling conntrack metrics in Prom. If we hit this again we'll need to automate node cordon/drain when conntrack > 90%.

maria_g: Small note: model-store already has keepalive but some older clients (batch jobs) don't. I'll add a backlog ticket to enforce pooled clients.

sre-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-118 opened: "eastus2 pod->pod connection resets due to conntrack exhaustion" — assigned to eng-platform and netops, priority P1.

vikram_s: After DaemonSet landed on gpunode-12 I can already see conntrack entries drop as some TIME_WAIT expired. Node went from 65k to 42k in ~6 minutes. Packets retransmit rate also decreased.

irene_p: Netops confirms MTU rollback completed across rack-3. Preliminary packet-loss graphs improved.

alex_kim: Good sign. Keeping this thread open for the next 24h. Will update INC and run a postmortem if we see recurrence. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

jamie: Postmortem checklist idea: list of mitigations (sysctl tuning, NAT capacity, connection pooling, MTU validation test in CI), and an automated alert when conntrack usage > 80% with suggested remediation playbook.

maria_g: Adding those to the ticket. I'll also add a quick smoke test to nightly GPU jobs to catch egress churn patterns early.

alex_kim: Closing loop: no new incidents for last 45m on the affected nodes. Leaving watch until 04:30 UTC.
